claim: VCO frequency-vs-VCTRL characterization of design/vco/vco_ring5.sch with the issue-#232 CLK buffer (design/clk-buf) driving the provisional 1 pF load defined in spec/decision-records/DR-008-clk-output-load-and-buffer-scope.md. The buffered sweep uses sim/vco's original six VCTRL values (0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.2, 1.4, 1.6 V) and the 45-point PVT grid from the unbuffered baseline, sim/vco/records/20260904-163130-f3ae976.md. The frequency difference at each matched (PVT, VCTRL) point measures the tuning shift caused by the buffer's input capacitance on the ring-side node. Measured design input only.
spec_rows_note: spec/target-spec.md row 2 (output band -- the free-running frequency this sweep reaches at each VCTRL point) and row 5 (Kvco -- the slope that frequency-vs-VCTRL curve defines), the two rows this manifest's own claim names. Both are DRAFT and owed a sky130 re-derivation; this is measured input to that, not a ratification.
methodology_note: For point-for-point comparison with the unbuffered baseline, this bench uses the same open-loop ring, sim/vco's original six VCTRL values, the `uic` startup kick, a 60 ns settling interval and default simulator options. The ring drives design/clk-buf, whose output drives the 1 pF DR-008 load. Measuring frequency on the ring-side net `vcoclk`, where the divider taps the ring in design/top, isolates the buffer's effect on tuning. Both benches use a 50 ps dump grid, so the upper-half VCTRL rows share the baseline's time-resolution limit.
analysis: one transient (`tran 50p 200n uic`) at each of sim/vco's original six VCTRL values to match the unbuffered baseline, with one ngspice invocation per PVT point
